pages.text: "Rain stopped! I'll cross the stepping stones to play!" Little brother Mumu threw open the mill door. Heavy rain had fallen all night. Puddles sparkled across the yard. He waddled toward the stream.
But the stream roared! Muddy yellow water rushed and overflowed. Not a stepping stone showed. All were underwater. As Mumu stretched a foot toward the edge, Dad caught him with a wing. "Wait!"
Dad crouched in front of Mumu, eye to eye. "The water has risen. All the stones are covered, right? At times like this, go up the bank." Mumu nodded. "Yes, Dad!"
Now they were up on the bank. Big sister Dodo was there too. Below, the wheel turned too fast, throwing white spray. Mumu and Dodo each held one of Dad's wings tight.

"Let's play baby birds in a nest." Dad tucked Mumu against his side and whispered, "The bank is a high nest. Water flows below; it can't reach the nest." Like a baby bird, Mumu stayed snug beside him.

Dad pointed one wing at the stream, the other at his side. "One, rising water, don't go near the stream! Two, up the bank beside Dad! Three, water goes down, go with a grown-up!" Mumu nodded. "Water rising? Up the bank!"
Mumu sat between Dad and Dodo on the bank, waiting for the water to fall. The stream still rushed. But with Dad, he wasn't afraid. Softly, he said, "Water rising? Up the bank!"
As the sun rose high, the water grew quieter. One stone appeared, then two. Dad held Mumu's wing. "Water's down. Let's go together." One tail flick. Mumu did it!

On the next day of heavy rain, Mumu ran up the bank first. "One, don't go near the stream! Two, up the bank beside Dad! Three, water goes down, go with a grown-up!" Looking back, he called, "Water rising? Up the bank!"
That evening, Dad hugged Mumu firmly in a wing. "Even with overflowing water, you came up the bank!" Rising water is okay when you go up the bank beside Dad. Mumu smiled. "Water rising? Up the bank!"
